title: Building Resilience Through Anxiety Virtual Education in PICU Survivors
official: BRAVE-PICU: Building Resilience Through Anxiety Virtual Education in PICU Survivors
summary: Survivors of Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) admissions often experience adverse mental health consequences, either as a result of, or associated with, their intensive care stay. Evidence-based digital cognitive behavioral therapy (dCBT) tools exist for both children and parents to learn cognitive behavioral strategies. In this feasibility study, we aim to measure the adoption and acceptability of a dCBT tool among PICU survivors and their parents. We hypothesize that \>50% of subjects will meet completion criteria for these programs, and that we will observe a trend toward improved anxiety scores.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age ≥ 7 and ≤ 13 (the dCBT program is only validated for patients within this age range)
* Admitted to the GCH PICU and have an anticipated discharge date in the subsequent 1 - 3 days
* Be able to interact with an iPad or computer device, as assessed by caregivers
* English speaking subjects due to the lack of translated versions of the dCBT tool

Exclusion Criteria:

* No specific exclusion criteria
